main_issue: Whether Agent D should finish the analysis section for Thursday's pitch (tonight, despite the bereavement) or whether a teammate should take it over

A-B.evidence: T3 A asks someone to take over D's section; T4 B refuses. T9 A urges D to finish tonight; T10 B says D should be with family. T13 B reluctantly says 'Okay' to D's plan, but without endorsing it.

A-C.evidence: T3 A asks for a teammate to get up to speed; T5 C declines ('I also can't take on your section'). C never addresses A's later push for D to finish tonight.

A-D.evidence: T6 D plans to finish tomorrow night; T7 A says that is too late. T8 D agrees to finish tonight, and T12 D reaffirms ('I'll work late, after. It has to be done'). A endorsed this in T9.

B-C.evidence: T4 B: 'I can't take this on.' T5 C: 'I also can't take on your section.' Both decline the handover and neither changes position.

B-D.evidence: T10 B: 'You should be with your family tonight.' T12 D: 'I'll be with my family. I'll work late, after.' T13 B only says 'Okay', so B's objection is not resolved.

C-D.evidence: T5 C declines the section; T6 D replies 'I understand. I have to be away.' C takes no further position after this, so the end alignment is unclear.
